story.role: a front-end developer rendering a list of people where some have no profile photo
story.want: a helper that turns a full name into its initials
story.benefit: avatar placeholders show consistent initials without each screen re-implementing the rule

impactedAreas.area: Public API of the text utilities (src/index.js)
impactedAreas.impact: Gains one new export, initials. No existing export changes, so current callers are unaffected.
The list of functions should mention initials.

task.goal: Add initials(name) to the text utilities so callers can derive upper-case initials from a person's name.

acceptance.behavior: The first character of each whitespace-separated word is returned, upper-cased with toUpperCase, in order. The first character is the first Unicode code point, kept whole, and a character with no upper-case form is returned as it is.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "ada lovelace"
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "AL"
And given the name "3d printer"
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "3P"
And given the name "😀 smile"
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "😀S"

acceptance.behavior: Leading, trailing and repeated whitespace between words is ignored. Whitespace means anything matched by the JavaScript regular expression \s.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "  grace   brewster  hopper "
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "GBH"

acceptance.behavior: A name with a single word returns one initial. An empty or blank name returns the empty string, and so do null and undefined. Any other non-string value is converted with String(name) first.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "plato"
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "P"
And given the name "   ", "", null or undefined
When initials is called with it
Then the result is ""
And given the number 42 as the name
When initials is called with it
Then the result is "4"

acceptance.behavior: An optional second argument, max, limits how many initials are returned, keeping the first ones. When max is given it must be a positive integer, and it is checked before the name is looked at, so an invalid max throws even for an empty name. When max is omitted or undefined there is no limit.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the name "grace brewster hopper" and max 2
When initials is called with them
Then the result is "GB"
And given the same name and max 5
When initials is called with them
Then the result is "GBH"
And given max 0, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity or the string "2", with any name including ""
When initials is called with them
Then a RangeError is thrown

acceptance.behavior: initials is exported from src/index.js alongside the existing functions.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a module that imports initials from src/index.js
When it calls initials("ada lovelace")
Then the result is "AL"

testCases.description: initials("ada lovelace") returns "AL"; initials("Ada Lovelace") also returns "AL".
initials("3d printer") returns "3P"; initials("😀 smile") returns "😀S", with the emoji kept whole.
initials("  grace   brewster  hopper ") returns "GBH"; a name separated by a tab and a newline, "a\tb\nc", returns "ABC".
initials("plato") returns "P"; initials(""), initials("   "), initials(null) and initials(undefined) all return ""; initials(42) returns "4".
initials("grace brewster hopper", 2) returns "GB"; with max 5 it returns "GBH"; with max omitted or undefined it returns "GBH".
initials("a b", bad) throws RangeError for each bad value in 0, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity and the string "2"; initials("", 0) and initials(null, 0) also throw RangeError, showing max is checked first.
The test file imports initials from ../src/index.js, so every test fails if the export is missing.
